Well, then, sir, I guess my question for you is: After these letters were sent in 1998, prior to the publication of your report, you did not send any additional letters to try and obtain input from the Yugoslav or Serbian authorities relative to specific charges of IHL, violations of international humanitarian law, that your organisation later claimed in the report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- these -- we did not send any letters after these letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So I think you're agreeing with me. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would it be fair to say then that your reports were generated without any information or input from the Yugoslav or Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not say that's fair to say. We used open-source material whenever possible to present the government view, and I sincerely wish that we had received responses to these letters from one of the many agencies and ministries to whom they were sent, to which they were sent, because I would have -- the report would have been strengthened greatly and all our work would have been strengthened greatly by having official answers to these particular inquiries.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you would concede, however, though, that that's another limitation of your report, that it's missing documentation, for instance, or official documentation from one of the parties in the conflict that you allege occurred?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We utilised all able information and in my view gave the governments of Serbia and Yugoslavia the opportunity to provide information, an opportunity that they declined.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you in your organisation, you did not have any formal mandate from the United Nations, the OSCE, the European Union in regard to dealings with the Serbian and Yugoslav authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your inquiries to the Yugoslav authorities came from a private source, from your private NGO. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a non-governmental organisation, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you will concede, I hope, that there were several internationally mandated organisations that were on the ground in Kosovo-Metohija who were in daily contact with the appropriate officials of the Serbian and Yugoslav organs who were mandated by the UN, the OSCE, and the European Union?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And perhaps the Yugoslav authorities, if they were in daily contact with these entities, perhaps the information that these entities received would have supplemented your report, would it not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you did not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, what are the entities you're thinking of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the Kosovo Verification Mission, and prior to that the Kosovo Diplomatic Observer Mission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that can't be what counsel is asking about because he's already been asking you questions to suggest you shouldn't have been relying on that information if it wasn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, I am asking about these organisations. There is other information that they had that somehow did not make it into their publications that is of great importance to this area of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But that's -- these are the only organisations you are thinking of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those are the two I am thinking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Counsel talked about several organisations mandated by, and he referred to the UN, the OSCE, and the European Union. But that's what we're talking about this -- the observer missions and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what I was assuming counsel was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe the -- KDOM, as it was called, that was a joint between the European Union and the UN. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe the UN --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It was a joint mission so that the entities that were involved would have been encompassed by the KVM, KDOM, and perhaps the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection is that the KDOM had a series of participating units. There was a US KDOM, there was an EU KDOM, and there was also a Russian KDOM.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, would it be fair to say that in a situation where there are -- we heard testimony -- we heard you testify to the nature of the skirmishes between the KLA and Serbian and Yugoslav forces on the ground in Kosovo-Metohija, would it be fair to say that the Yugoslav authorities perhaps had their hands full with other matters insofar as they were giving daily reports to these official organisations perhaps did not have time to respond to every private inquiry such as those from your organisation?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot speculate as to the workload of the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But that does not defy logic, does it?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Does what defy logic, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My proposition that perhaps they were not able to respond to every private inquiry insofar as they had their hands full on the ground and they were giving daily reports to a handful of internationally recognised organisations that were essentially doing the same task.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether the authorities responded to us or not was their decision, and we had not mandate to force their compliance in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just to clear up something that you testified to I believe actually earlier today. Are you familiar with the general terms of the OSCE agreement by which the Kosovo Verification Mission came to Kosovo and the interactions between, for instance, the Serbian police and the KVM?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the general contours of that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you if you're familiar with this. Are you familiar with the fact that that agreement specified certain police activities, including check-points, that were on the territory of Kosovo-Metohija?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if you for a moment take me at my word, if I can present for you what for you is a hypothetical since you don't have the knowledge. If in fact the agreement called for the police to undertake certain activities such as check-points or perpetuated such activities, would the KLA's attack of those posts be in your view a legitimate or illegitimate act, in view of your discussions earlier today regarding attacks on police officers?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends what you mean by "legitimate."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, what do you mean by "legitimate"? As a violation of -- is it a terrorist act?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A terrorist act, no. Is it a hostility and is that police check-point a legitimate target under IHL?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would depend on the function of that check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And again, since you don't have knowledge of the OSCE agreement we can't really go much further into that, right?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat what we said prior to the break, which is that a check-point for traffic purposes, for instance, would not be considered a legitimate military target but one that had -- that contributed to the -- to the ongoing hostilities in some way would be considered.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I guess what I'm trying to get at is: Illegitimate targets are not limited just to traffic police and traffic stops. Is that correct? There's a whole wide range of other potential police functions that would be illegitimate targets under IHL for the KLA, or for any other armed group for that matter. You're just using the traffic police as a clear example?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not a lawyer, but my understanding of the law is that it's the term direct participation in hostilities, that is the threshold with which one judges whether a target is legitimate or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So insofar as you are not a lawyer, would that then -- would that qualification have to apply to all the other legal conclusions that you have testified to, such as your claim that there was an armed conflict, for instance?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That claim is the position of the organisation which was reached after ongoing consultations within Human Rights Watch, which included our legal team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the other week you testified relative to a tragic incident in Gornje Obrinje which occurred, I believe you said, in September of 1998. First of all, the site of the incident in question, that is extremely close to an area that was a KLA stronghold in 1998. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was -- the KLA had a base, if you can call it, in the nearby village of Likovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm referring to. Now, and isn't it also true that the area saw fierce combat between the KLA and the Serbian forces immediately prior to the discovery of the bodies of the victims?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was combat between the two sides, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And isn't it also fair to say that there was fierce combat, or at least hostilities, even subsequent to the discovery of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that the hostilities were ongoing for at least two days prior to the discovery of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about subsequent to, sir.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Subsequent to?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The discovery of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh. Okay. Now, in fact, around the time that you were in the area, I believe on 30 September 1998, isn't it true that an International Red Cross vehicle on the road heading toward Gornje Obrinje was attacked and disabled by the KLA and pinned down?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the precise date of that incident, but I do recall the incident, also because I observed the ICRC vehicle. And what precisely happened is that this Land Rover, if I'm not mistaken, struck a land-mine on the road between Gornje Obrinje and Likovac and at least one, I believe it was an ethnic Albanian doctor, was killed in the blast. And another vehicle from the KDOM, if I'm not mistaken, Canadian, also struck a land-mine in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And wasn't it a fact, sir, that they were pinned down by KLA fire so that they had to be evacuated by a Serbian MUP helicopter and a detachment of Serbian MUP forces?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But in fact you do actually have the reporting of the Red Cross vehicle being destroyed and of the casualties that ensued in Under Orders. That's published in that report as well, is it not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I observed that vehicle myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. But your description of the International Red Cross vehicle being struck -- of striking the mine and of being -- and of the casualties resulting from this KLA action, that didn't appear in your publication regarding the Drenica valley, Week of Terror in Drenica, did it?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check, but that report, the Week of Terror in Drenica, is very explicit in the degree of fighting that took place in and around Gornje Obrinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My point is, sir, that you were an eye-witness to the tragedy that befell the International Red Cross at the hands of the KLA but you did not publish that until 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I would have to look back into the Week of Terror in Drenica report, but we mentioned in that report that up to 12 Serbian policemen died in fighting in Gornje Obrinje. And I'd have to check that precise number, but that's my recollection. So I believe we were very upfront that hostilities were taking place. And secondly, my information is that the ICRC vehicle struck a land-mine, and I did not know -- I have no information that they were pinned down by KLA fire. That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Now, would it be fair to say that under such circumstances the area around Gornje Obrinje was, at the very least, a contested area if not under the control of the KLA and out of effective control of the legitimate government forces of Serbia or Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA had an established presence in Likovac and the area and was active around Gornje Obrinje at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And without effective control of Gornje Obrinje and with the presence of the KLA there, that would make it very difficult for the Serbian authorities to carry out any investigations of the Gornje Obrinje site, would it not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an attempt by an international team to conduct an exhumation of the Gornje Obrinje site. This was a Finnish forensic team headed by Dr. Helena Ranta.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. And they were also -- the convoy was also -- included certain pathologists from the Serbian authorities as well. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that is accurate, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And isn't it also accurate that due to the threat of the KLA in the area, that convoy could not proceed and could not complete exhumations and investigations?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, if other witnesses state so, we'll find out. But, sir, the question I have for you is: Are you aware of the fact the Serbian authorities, and in particular the judiciary, issued an official inquiry and authorised an exhumation and directed the police to carry out the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Again this brings us back to the point that your publications suffer from a deficiency that they don't have all of the information relative to the events that are being reported.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you about the exhumation in Gornje Obrinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you answer my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me read it once again then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We provided the Serbian and Yugoslav governments and the relevant officials with the opportunity to provide us with information. They declined to do so. We relied then on the public and open sources that were available at that time to present and provide information that gave the government's view. And I wish that we had received more information from the authorities so that they could have been included in our reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, if there is information from the Serbian authorities showing their activities to investigate things that occurred even before your publication was published in February of 1999, we're talking about the Week of Terror in Drenica, that would very much change the conclusions contained in your report, would it not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As to the inaction of the Serbian authorities in attempts to carry out investigations?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall us reporting that they failed to investigate what -- this specific incident. What we reported in the Week of Terror in Drenica report was what we concluded was an attempt to block the Finnish forensic team from accessing the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, you did not have the information that might have changed those conclusions?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did have the information from individuals in the Finnish convoy that Serbian police forces prevented them from accessing the Gornje Obrinje area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You were not physically present to eye-witness any of this?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I relied on interviews with the Finnish team, as well as villagers in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, for instance, also would it be fair to say that you did not have at your disposal information regarding the number of investigations or criminal charges or indictments levied by the Serbian authorities, that is to say investigations by the Serbian MUP, official criminal charges filed with the Prosecutor's office, et cetera, for the period of July 1st, 1998 through to June 1st, 1999 dealing with crimes committed by various individuals against victims of Kosovo Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We asked for that information in some of these letters and it was not provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you do not have any information regarding the fact that over a thousand such criminal charges were prepared by the Serbian authorities against alleged perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have knowledge of that precise number, but I take no issue whatsoever with the Serbian and Yugoslav government's right and, indeed, their obligation to prosecute crimes within the territory under their authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You would agree, would you not, however, that knowledge of these facts would be instrumental to some of the conclusions that you draw in your various reports regarding the culpability of various state organs in crimes that you allege occurred?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with that, no. I believe we have collected evidence that documents very serious crimes by the Serbian police in the case of your client, and the evidence speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But again, that evidence is missing a key element as to what was done afterwards by the authorities.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so. I believe we have documented accurately both the actions and subsequent inactions that surrounded the incidents we cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you earlier testified that the source of your information regarding Gornje Obrinje were I believe the persons who happened to cross and discover the bodies. Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our research into Gornje Obrinje relied on -- primarily with interviewing individuals who found the bodies in the forest, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact these persons did not -- were not eye-witnesses to the actual killings themselves, were they?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in fact I believe in your report you state that these persons fled the area and only found the bodies when they returned?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, therefore when it comes to the bodies in the forest, wouldn't it be more honest to say that the accounts of their death are based on speculation and guesses because these people were not eye-witnesses to the actual killings, that there is a degree of speculation there?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. Our conclusions are based on more than two weeks -- in fact, I believe it's three weeks of extremely rigorous research. And when the body of evidence is taken in its entirety, which includes the testimony of multiple witnesses, plus our examination of the crime scene, plus the fact that hostilities did take place, we reached the conclusions in our report, namely that these individuals were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, there were no eye-witnesses to the killings in the forest, were there?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody saw the precise killings, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Nobody saw the perpetrators performing the acts alleged?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: People saw the perpetrators in and around the area, but nobody witnessed the perpetrators pulling the trigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, correct me if I'm wrong, you've already clarified that you are not legally trained, but am I also correct to say that you have no formal training or education as a police investigator or as a police officer?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You have no formal training or education as a forensic pathologist?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have what I would call preliminary forensic training, meaning I've been -- that I have what I would consider a good knowledge of basic forensics, but I do not have a formal education in forensic science.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You have not had any formal training or education as a criminal technician?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- so therefore your opinions or conclusions as to how these individuals died and in what means they died are of limited value in that regard. They're just your personal, untrained, unqualified conclusions?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I take issue with the word "untrained," but I will say this. We have made every effort in all of our reporting to state what we know and what we don't know. Everything has a footnote. Everything is cited. We're upfront about the limitations on our data, and the reports speak for themselves. We will allow the readers to reach conclusions based on the facts as we have provided them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Abrahams, in any event you are aware of instances where the KLA killed ethnic Albanian civilians, are you not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you are also familiar with the efforts of the KLA to try and obtain intervention from the outside world against the Serbian and Yugoslav forces, particularly in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you clarify what you mean by "obtain intervention."

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Military intervention.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that the KLA was interested in getting, particularly NATO, involved in the conflict, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And isn't it also a fact that your organisation made a finding or a conclusion that for propaganda purposes the KLA intentionally provoked attacks against Albanian civilians to try and gain such intervention from NATO?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusion you are referring to can be categorised as such. I believe that the KLA was aware of the -- of the need to win public opinion and that the unfortunate crimes and the abuses against ethnic Albanians were for them -- they had an interest in getting that information out to the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, I think it's a little more than that. I believe your organisation stated, and I can direct you to Under Orders, which is P438, e-court it's page 80, and this is again repeated at page 130 as well. And I believe I'm quoting your organisation in saying: "In the very least, the KLA understood the political benefit of civilian casualties."

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's exactly what I just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe that the -- isn't it a fact that we can -- we cannot exclude the possibility that the Gornje Obrinje tragedy was at the hands of the KLA, since there were no eye-witnesses?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I collected no such information to lead me to that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you interview Imer Delilaj?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the family of the victims in Gornje Obrinje, was he not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you interviewed him on November 10th, 1998?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Interviewed him on more than one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And, by the way, Imer was a self-avowed fighter in the KLA, was he not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in lamenting the death of his brother, one of the victims, he reported to you -- and this is also in -- this is in Exhibit P441, in e-court page 36. Why don't we wait for that to come up on the screen, sir. It might be easier for you, sir, to comment on where I'm going to now. Page 36 on the e-court. If you could scroll down. Is this 36? I'm showing 1 of 1 on my -- this is not the page. I'll see if I can get the ERN number. That might assist us. The ERN number is K0364957. That appears to be the page. If we can zoom in on the indented text in the middle of the page and in particular the last two lines of that indented text, sir. This is your recitation of your interview with Mr. Imer Delilaj. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you scroll up a touch?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You want to see the bottom of the page, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this is okay, Your Honour. Yes, I believe this is a citation from my interview with Imer Delilaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if you could focus your attention again to the last two lines of this where I believe the statement is: "Adem was 33 years old and had never been armed in his life. He never had problems with the government or the KLA." Now, Mr. Abrahams, my question for you is: Doesn't this statement from Mr. Delilaj, himself a member of the KLA and was knowledgeable about the KLA's activities, seem to imply that it was possible for ethnic Albanians to have a threat from the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, we have acknowledged and documented that some ethnic Albanians did have problems with the KLA, and how this statement is read, I suppose, open for interpretation, but one interpretation could be the conclusion you've reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would that interpretation -- strike that. Would people living in Gornje Obrinje who perhaps knew of attacks or killings by the KLA of ethnic Albanians be able to view -- to view this as saying that there are two potential culprits for these killings, namely the government forces or the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. If we have knowledge of killings by the KLA in Gornje Obrinje of ethnic Albanians that predate this instance, then we would have to conclude, would we not, that there are two potential culprits for the killings in this particular case as well?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard information about ethnic Albanians killed by the KLA in Gornje Obrinje. That is -- I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So again we come back to the point that you -- your reports lack critical information relating to the events that are reported?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't lack information if that information doesn't exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: May I have Exhibit 6D12 up on the screen, please. It should be 6D12 -- I think the transcript has -- okay, now it's corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is the English translation of a document, the original of which is also in the e-court system in Serbian. This is an onsite investigative report dated 13th February, 1998 in the village of Gornje Obrinje, is it not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And it regards the murder of postman Mustafa Kurtaj, does it not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And based upon your knowledge of -- of the people there and the languages spoken, can you make any conclusions regarding the ethnicity of this victim?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kurtaj is an Albanian name, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if you read further it would appear that this document talks about the fact that Mr. Kurtaj was killed in the region, the same region that you specified, does it not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And again this is information that you did not have in your possession at the time that you created your report?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And he was a postman. Are you familiar with attacks by the KLA against postmen who were doing their job within the legitimate structures of the Serbian and Yugoslav governmental organs?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically against postmen I'm not aware of cases, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would a attack on a postman --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just a matter of clarification. The question itself, terms of the question is not necessarily improper. But the question is asked with this document on the screen, so therefore there is an issue as to whether or not the question is connected with the document, i.e., the question asks about KLA killing of postmen. Is that question related to something in this document? Is that the reason we have this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have this document to talk about a killing of an ethnic Albanian in Gornje Obrinje which the witness said he did not have knowledge of such things occurring, and now I'm moving on to separate issue talking about legitimacy of attacks on governmental organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But perhaps if counsel could assist us by showing us where he said he had no knowledge of the killings -- of any killing of ethnic Albanians in Gornje Obrinje. I think he said that he had not knowledge of any ethnic Albanian being killed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He didn't say he had no knowledge of ethnic Albanians being killed at all. Now the question refers to the killing of an ethnic Albanian postman by the KLA. Is that question related to this document. That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In part, but I'm moving beyond the document. That was just to -- since he says he has no knowledge of this, I cannot ask him about this specific instance. I'm asking him more generally speaking if he was aware of postmen being attacked by the KLA. I believe he has answered that. And now I would just ask him a general question, if in fact there were facts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do that, can I just be clear. This translation is accurate in respect that this is a postman, that's a person who delivers letters?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not simply a SUP officer occupying a particular post. It's someone who actually delivers letters, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's my understanding that it is someone who delivers letters. But since this witness doesn't have knowledge about the specifics --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I wasn't aware so far that the SUP dealt with the delivery of letters, but that's now expanding my knowledge of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The SUP does not, Your Honour, but postal services is also an organ of the Serbian government, public enterprise, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, no doubt it will become clear in due course. But continue with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, first of all, sir, do you have knowledge of the fact that the postal service in Kosovo-Metohija was a -- was viewed by the KLA as being part of the government of the Serbian authorities in your interviews with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Specifically about the postal service, no, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Would you -- would you consider attacks against postal service employees to be legitimate or illegitimate under IHL?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour, but there's a very odd siren in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think we all hear it. It's outside.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. It's a bit distracting, if I may -- okay. Sorry. I thought it was just in the headphones. No, I would not consider attacks on postal workers legitimate under IHL, unless that postal worker was actively engaged in hostilities. But by definition, postal workers are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough, sir. Now, let's turn for a moment to the historical presentations in your various reports, and I believe you indicated that during your time period with the Office of the Prosecutor you were primarily engaged in the historical aspects of the indictment, the background, historical background. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regards to the indictment in particular?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as far as the historical presentations in your reports and in the indictment, you did not -- you have no formal education in Balkan history, do you?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My degree is in international studies, a master's degree, with a focus on eastern Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. How many professors of Balkan history were employed by Human Rights Watch, if any, in the drafting of these reports?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Employed? None.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: None. Okay. During the vetting process that you described earlier, did any professors of Balkan history review and make comment on the historical sections of your reports?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe so, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For that matter, during the vetting process did you have any police experts review your reports and offer any criticism thereupon?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's your definition of a police expert?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, someone who -- let's break it down to several categories. Did you have anyone -- did you have any police instructors in any accredited police academies or police colleges as part of the vetting process?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have any high-ranking members of police forces, national police forces, anywhere outside of the Balkans as part of the vetting process?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have any authors, distinguished authors who had written upon the topic of police activities and police structures as part of your vetting process?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, returning to the time period when you worked for the Prosecutor of this very same Tribunal, would it be accurate to say that your work at the Office of the Prosecutor assisted that office in preparing the indictment, at least the historical part of the indictment against Mr. Milosevic, that in essence is part of the -- part of these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify my role. When I arrived here, the indictment had already been issued and the Office of the Prosecutor was in the process of amending the indictment. So I was asked to assist by collecting or by pointing the team in the right direction to where they might collect the documentation to bolster these -- to bolster the historical claims. I also want to state that that was -- that was just one of my -- one of my tasks and not a primary -- not a primary one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, at that time, however, the indictment against the -- against these accused had not yet been formulated and issued. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My recollection is the -- that the Milosevic indictment included some of the individuals here today but not all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Not all. Okay. And wouldn't it be fair to say, sir, that in generating your reports you stated that it was a very important objective to assist the process of investigations against Serbian Yugoslav officials for the events in Kosovo-Metohija?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the primary objectives of our documentation is to promote the interests of international justice, and towards that aim we hope our material will assist the tribunal, this Tribunal, in its investigations and prosecutions against all who are alleged to have violated the law, regardless of their ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And that objective, to essentially investigate events that would lead to prosecution of Serb officials, that was the main objective of taking interviews from persons in Kukes and wherever else the interviews were conducted. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one of many objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But it was an objective?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And isn't it a fact, sir, that these interviews that were undertaken and that are -- that portions or summaries of which are reproduced in our various publications, such as Under Orders, are not or were not taken under oath?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under oath, no. No, they were not taken under oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They were not -- there was no court officer to swear the witness in?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: They were not subject to the penalty of perjury, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, furthermore your reports have not provided or disclosed much of the source material for the summaries of the interviews as well as the identities of many of the interviewees. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of the interviews in our reports are cited. On some occasions to protect the identity of witnesses who requested protection due to fear of reprisals, we would use initials or some other method to protect their full identity. But I would have to go through the footnotes to tell you how -- what percentage of the witnesses requested that protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In any event, your organisation did not do any significant background checks of these interviewees to ascertain any connection with the KLA or any bias resulting therefrom, did you?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our research relied on as many witnesses as possible to obtain an accurate picture of events, and to do so we witnessed multiple victims and -- excuse me, we interviewed multiple victims and witnesses, asking detailed questions to corroborate the information that -- that they provided. So if you are asking whether we obtained that -- legal documents to describe this person's full history, no, we did not. But we conduct our interviews in such a way that we can, as best as possible, confirm, verify, and corroborate the information they provide.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, isn't it true that the KLA which was mainly based in villages was primarily based around familial units?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'll have to explain what you mean by that so I can answer correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure. Would it be fair to say that in particular villages there would be particular families who were in the KLA and particular families that were not in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would, in general, agree with that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're talking generally.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, families would participate or would not participate, but there certainly were occasions where one brother would and one brother wouldn't, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. But again, generally speaking, isn't it true that the familial patriarch, that is the leading male figure in the family, would have a great deal of say or control over the remaining members of that family?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you also agree that if the familial patriarch was a member of the KLA or sympathised with the KLA, he would have control or pressure over his remaining family members regarding what they talk about with respect to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe that you, yourself, or your organisation have knowledge or reached an understanding that the KLA did have a history of pressuring people with regards to what was presented to the media and to outsiders. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were cases where the KLA would exert its influence on individuals in Kosovo. So, yes, that did take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact this is a concern that you cited I believe in Under Orders, if I'm accurate, if not I can get you the page number. But I believe that you stated that your -- you had reached the knowledge and understanding that the KLA had instructed people not to speak about certain events to the media and to other people interviewing them. Is that -- do you recall that, or do we need to get to the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be better to get to the exhibit, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's Under Orders, I believe that's P438, and I believe this appears at page 22 on the e-court variant. I believe this is not page 22 on e-court. Let me -- let me try and get the e-court number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is there. "In some cases they had been instructed by the KLA not to speak of certain events." That's not the one you're looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That -- that, I think, is, but I'm not seeing it on the screen. Ah, there it is in the middle. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, now, does that assist you in answering my prior question, which I believe was: Is it accurate that your organisation found that the KLA had instructed people not to speak about certain events?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In certain cases, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And, sir, wouldn't it be a logical by-product of that conclusion and understanding that if the KLA told people what not to speak about, there could very well have been instances where the KLA told people precisely what to speak about.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer to that question is -- you'll have to bear with me, it's a little complex. Because that is precisely why we conduct interviews in such a detailed fashion, so that there is no way possible that an investigation like into Gornje Obrinje that lasted for three weeks and involved interviews with multiple witnesses in one-on-one settings could have been coordinated from above because we ask such specific questions. For example, what was the weather like at that moment? What was he or she wearing at that moment? Questions which sometimes seem inane but allow us to reveal inconsistencies, inconsistencies which undermine the credibility of the witnesses, and that is exactly why this research takes as long as it does. So in the case of Gornje Obrinje, we did that research, we followed that methodology, and we reached the conclusions that we've presented in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I think we've already reached the understanding or conclusion that there was no direct testimony in Gornje Obrinje regarding the perpetrators, so I think we can put that aside. I'm focussing on Under Orders which talks about the results of the interviews in Kukes, which I referenced earlier, which I believe were refugees in the various centres there and the reporting or the conclusions of why they left their homes that I was making reference to. Would it be a logical by-product of the Human Rights Watch finding that the KLA had instructed people what not to speak about, that it also instructed them on what to speak of in place of what not to speak about?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: While there may be isolated incidents of what we could call coaching, I am firmly of the belief that this did not happen on a systematic level or in a coordinated manner because the exodus of more than 850.000 people was so chaotic and so violent that people were flowing across the borders with none of their possessions and moving quickly into different refugee camps in Macedonia and in northern Albania. And there is no way that the KLA or any other force could have instructed them in such a systematic manner to give consistent and reliable reports of the nature you're suggesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And your interviews were in Kukes which is near a KLA base, is it not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interviews were in Kukes and there are KLA bases in northern Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in fact I believe in Under Orders you reach the conclusion that any evidence coming either directly or indirectly from the KLA heightened your suspicions about its accuracy. Is that a fair assessment of your findings, or your belief I should say?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We view information coming from any -- any official source or any party to the armed conflict with a healthy dose of suspicion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And would it be fair to say that you cannot -- first of all, you only interviewed 600 persons from one of the centres. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, "one of the centres"?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In Kukes. From Kukes, not from other -- from Macedonia, for instance, or ...

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again I take issue with the descriptive "only." I consider it --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's take out "only." You interviewed 600 individuals in our preparation of your findings, or your report?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In both Albania and Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You did not interview the 800.000 that you cited before?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We interviewed 600.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You interviewed a limited group in a limited area that had KLA activity, at least part of it, Kukes?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we would have to go through -- no. The 600 individuals who were interviewed, they were interviewed in different areas, which is in northern Albania, as well as in other parts of Albania, like Tirana, the capital, as well as in Macedonia. And furthermore, we returned to Kosovo in June 1999 and continued our investigations precisely with the objective of investigating further the reports we received from refugees during the war. So we went back to the villages that they told us about to find -- to investigate the scenes, to interview more witnesses. And that is part of the 600. And one point I want to stress is I was continually amazed by the degree of consistency between the reports of refugees and our findings when returning down to the degree of specific names. So refugees, for example, would tell us that in such-and-such a village 11 people were killed, ethnic Albanians, were killed by Serbian forces, and they would give us the names. And when we returned to that village, we found precisely the same number of people and the same names. So I was quite astounded by the degree of corroboration we found between the refugee accounts and our onsite investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, let's return back to the KLA for a second, since that was my question. Let's take a step back to 1998 and 1999. I believe you've already confirmed that there were -- or at least acknowledged that there were frequent attacks on the part of the KLA against, first of all, civilians of all nationalities and then against legitimate government forces and then against army forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends what time-frame you are referring to because --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 1998 through 1999 is what I specified.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, we need to be more precise, because we have documented crimes by the KLA against ethnic Serbs and Albanians in 1998. No question about it. It's all there in our reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period of 1999, specifically the period of the NATO bombing, we do not have documentation of KLA abuses during that time. The explanation of course is that they -- it was the period of the NATO bombing and the KLA was otherwise engaged, was in hiding, was active in fighting. So we don't have evidence of abuses against civilians at that specific time, March through June 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, isn't it a fact that -- strike that. First of all, let's talk about 1998 and then we'll get to 1999. Isn't it a fact that in 1998 the KLA on the 40 per cent of the territory that it controlled did regularly or -- let's not even say regularly, but did significantly engage in a campaign of violence against civilians of all nationalities and ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I prefer to be specific. It is true in a number of serious incidents the KLA abducted and killed ethnic Serbs as well as ethnic Albanians in places such as Orahovac, in places such as the Belacevac mine and in and around -- in the Djakovica area. It happened, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if you want, let's go specific, if you'd like to, as an example. Isn't it true that on September 9th, 1998 near the Kosovo town of Glodane the bodies of 34 civilians, victims of the KLA, were found in a lake. Do you recall that instance?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And isn't it also likewise true that -- first of all, are you familiar with the so-called October accords that were entered into in October 1998, the cease-fire?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar of its existence but not its details.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware of the fact or do you have knowledge of the fact that the KLA repeatedly violated that cease-fire agreement subsequent to October of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, without -- without knowing the details of the agreement, I can't say whether they violated it. But if you're asking whether the KLA engaged in hostilities after October 1998, they did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And if we were to look even earlier, you would have to agree, would you not, that even as early as 1996 the KLA was organised in or was engaged in pre-planned violence against both civilians and the civil authorities, would you not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA began its military operations or its hostilities in Kosovo in 1996, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact you summarise some of that in Under Orders. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you have knowledge, then, I presume, regarding the funding and support base of the KLA and that one source was this Homeland Calling fund which levied attacks on Albanians in the diaspora, would you not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with the organisation Homeland Calling, but I, to my knowledge, I would not call it attacks but they collected contributions from the diaspora on a voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And are you familiar with pressure or violence used against persons who refused to contribute to this -- to this fund, if you will?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. In addition to the fund, the KLA was founded and drew its support from other activities, including drug smuggling, human trafficking, money laundering, and other criminal activities? Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Don't answer that for the moment. Mr. Ivetic, can you help us with the purpose of these questions. Where is it they are leading?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What I'm leading to, Your Honour, is that this witness gave some testimony going around how to qualify the KLA. He wouldn't call them terrorists. He wanted to call them insurgents. I'm trying to find out what his definition of the KLA encompasses. And the words I'm using right now come from his report, so I'm not trying to place any words in his mouth that he hasn't already uttered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just give me a moment then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We see the legitimate purpose for which these questions are being asked. But I think, Mr. Ivetic, it's also legitimate for us to invite you to get more quickly to the point rather than explore in detail activities of the KLA of which we are fairly well aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. I will try to abbreviate my discussion of that. I'm directed to the clock. Should we -- do we need to take a pause or can we continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, since we're near the break I just want to address a question to you to my colleague to ask if we can have an estimate for how much for purposes of scheduling witnesses. We have got one with a young baby and one with a medical condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you help, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I should have about 45 to 50 more questions which I would estimate would be about an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'll try to be a little less, obviously. I'll try and use the break to cull my questions to be more succinct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll take the break now and we'll resume at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.28 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Abrahams, I'd like to first return for just a brief moment to Gornje Obrinje, since I had an opportunity to review the transcript and saw that I'd missed one critical element. Namely, are you aware that after the Serbian judicial authorities ordered an investigation and an exhumation, and that while the forensic pathologists and criminal technicians were on their way under the security of the police, because obviously the police does not perform the exhumation, they provide security, are you aware that the convoy itself was shot at in Likovica [phoen], an area that you previously identified as a base for KLA activity?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That information is not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You would agree, would you not, that that bit of information would have a significant bearing on conclusions relating to Gornje Obrinje and whether or not the authorities were responsive to complaints about that incident?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: A significant bearing, no, I would not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You would agree that it has some impact on your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the government was in good faith making an effort to investigate the crime with an eye towards prosecuting those responsible, then, yes, that is a -- that is a -- that would --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would change things --

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would -- sorry, I'm still digesting my lunch. I apologise. Then that would be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That would be relevant. Okay. And again, this is information that you did not have.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the authorities had sent a delegation or sent a forensic team?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct, and that they were shot upon and could not proceed due to the shootings in -- from the direction of Likovic?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could return for a moment to the issue of the KLA. We had talked before the break about some of the activities of the KLA. As someone who has studied the region and has some knowledge on it, are you familiar with another organisation that helped recruit fighters for the KLA called the Albanian Arab Islamic Bank?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you aware with statements made by Mr. Fatos Klosi, the former head of the Albanian intelligence service in 1998, that this organisation and other al Qaeda terrorist cells were sending fighters to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that statement, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was that part -- you did not -- strike that. I take it, then, that was not part of your research for your book on history where you claim that the KLA was distancing itself from terrorists?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For my research, I actually interviewed Mr. Klosi, Fatos Klosi to whom you refer, and further investigated the claims of Islamic fighters, but at no point did I encounter statements from him about this bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did he mention al Qaeda fighters?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Al Qaeda, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Terrorists?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to -- are you aware with the French national Claude Kader who was arrested in France in 1998 and was -- and testified that he personally trained and recruited al Qaeda fighters for the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with that name, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And are you aware with the subject matter of his testimony as I have summarised it?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of that case, but my recollection is not precise, is that Mr. Claude Kader was arrested in Tirana for murdering an Albanian, I believe his translator, if I'm not mistaken. And in the course of his testimony he said that he had been hired to recruit Islamic fighters for the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the point of all these questions is, sir, you stated earlier that you tend to avoid classifying the KLA as a terrorist group but rather call it insurgency. But wouldn't it be fair to say that whether you coin the KLA as a terrorist group or an insurgency, or just some type of organised criminal element, you would have to qualify their activities of attacking civilians, including civilians of all nationalities, including non-Serbs and non-Albanians, such as Goranje [phoen], Roma, Turks, Egyptians, et cetera, that those would constitute criminal acts by any definition, would they not?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that the KLA's attacks on legitimate military targets during the state of armed conflict were not violations of international humanitarian law but they could be categorised, classified, and prosecuted as violations of Serbian or Yugoslav law. Now, attacks on illegitimate targets, such as civilians, would, in addition to being violations of domestic law, also be a violation of international humanitarian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And wouldn't you also have to agree that eliminating such criminal activity, be it quantified as terrorism or other criminal acts, and stopping those engaged in the abduction and/or killing of civilians is a legitimate function and obligation of any state, not just Serbia or federal Yugoslavia as it was at the time?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and my work is not whether a state does that, but how the state does that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe you've mentioned that before. Now, I believe that you testified the other week before the break that you could agree that there was -- that in general there was some degree of intimidation upon the ethnic Albanian population from the side of the KLA. Now I'm going to ask you a different question. Are you aware of the fact that the KLA also engaged in some conflict with other organised Kosovo Albanian groups, armed or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And of which -- of which groups are you aware of, that were in conflict with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one group I know of is called the FARK, Forcat e Armatosura e Republikes se Kosoves.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We're on the same wavelength, that's where I was heading. And this so-called FARK, the English translation being the armed forces of the republic of Kosova, I believe, this was headed by Bujar Bukoshi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bukoshi had a role in FARK to the best of my knowledge, but I'm not sure if he was the leader or -- what word did you use?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I used the word "head." I believe -- let me quantify that. Mr. Bukoshi was the self-styled Prime Minister of the self-proclaimed government in exile of the Kosovo Albanians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't call him self-styled. I believe he was the chosen Prime Minister in that government. Whether you view that government as legal or not is another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, that government wasn't recognised by any states, was it?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, isn't it also true that FARK had armed units within the territory of Kosovo-Metohija during the relevant time period 1998, 1999?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were periods when FARK had armed units in Kosovo, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And isn't it also true that FARK's armed units clashed with those of the so-called KLA?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were incidents of so-called clashes, but I'm not aware of the extent. And at a certain point there was a cessation of hostilities between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At a certain point, they merged. Some elements merged. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But in fact the -- there is some intimation that FARK's military leader, Ahmet Krasniqi, who was assassinated in Tirana in September of 1998 had been assassinated by KLA supporters. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many allegations about why Mr. Krasniqi was murdered in Tirana, and I, through my investigations with Human Rights Watch and my book, have never been able to determine who the perpetrator was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But that is one of the theories that's out there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the KLA killed Mr. Krasniqi? That is one of the theories, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in addition, the KLA was also at odds with the LDK, which was the political party that Mr. Rugova headed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The LDK political party and the KLA had different views on how to resolve the Kosovo issue, and those views were often at odds with one other, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in addition to being at odds with one another, isn't it also true that there were reported instances of the KLA harassing or beating up LDK officials who were advocating for a peaceful solution rather than a military solution?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are some cases of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you are aware of them?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to say then also that the civilian population, the Kosovo Albanian civilian population, likewise would be split up amongst these various affiliations or support for these various groups?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends what time period you're speaking about. Because popular support for the LDK, Ibrahim Rugova, and that political party was very strong leading up to 1998, but it was eroding over time as the abuses continued and as the militant organisation of the KLA, the armed group of the KLA, began to present itself as an alternative to the LDK. And as the abuses continued, the moderate politicians or the politicians who were pursuing the non-violent approach in the LDK, and Rugova specifically, were losing ground to the militants who said: This policy is not working and we must confront the Serbian state with force. And in particular, I would point to the events of Drenica in late February/early March 1998 when in a series of incidents Serbian forces killed 85 individuals, among them more than 20 women and children. And in my opinion, this was a watershed moment when public opinion shifted from the LDK to the KLA, viewing the armed insurgency as both a means of defence and also the only viable option to confront the aggression -- what they viewed as the aggression of the Serbian state.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That being said, though, sir, I'm sure you can't deny that there maintains some tensions if not open hostility and conflict between these various ethnic Kosovo Albanian groups who had differing agendas and differing plans for how to obtain those agendas. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many different views and a constant tension between the groups, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, turning back to the areas that you previously testified that IHL violations are alleged to have occurred or that from where the interviewees came from, isn't it fair to say that these areas that you previously mentioned, these several municipalities, were areas where there were a significant number of armed exchanges between the so-called KLA, terrorist or otherwise, and the legitimate police and army forces of Serbia and Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some cases, yes, and in some cases, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general -- excuse me. In general there were violations in areas where the KLA was active; that is absolutely true. But we also documented cases where the KLA had no activity. For example, in the city of Pec or in the city of Pristina or in districts like Istok and Lipljan where KLA activity was significantly less.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's focus on those areas where KLA activity vis-a-vis the legitimate police and army forces was prevalent. Would it be -- and you've already -- I believe we've already discussed the fact that the KLA had no problem initiating attacks from villages knowing that civilians would get caught in the middle. Would it -- under those circumstances, would it be fair to say that the average Kosovo Albanian had reason to fear for their safety, given these inter-party clashes between the legitimate police and army forces on the one hand, and the KLA, whatever you want to call them, on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first I would say that on occasion the KLA put the civilian population at risk by launching attacks from populated areas. I wouldn't say that they did it with the purpose or the aim of opening this population to attack, but there were cases when their actions did have that result due to the overreaction from the Serbian police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In that situation then, wouldn't -- strike that. You cannot exclude, then, that some people that left those municipalities left as a direct and proximate result of the ongoing fighting that was going on between the so-called KLA and the legitimate state forces?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What time period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are very different periods. This was a dynamic conflict in which the conditions changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, what about in areas where the KLA was feuding with FARK or other Kosovo Albanian organisations, wouldn't it be logical and possible that people would flee to avoid that conflict as well?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tension and conflict between KLA and FARK was limited to the areas in the far west of the country along the border with Albania. And to my knowledge, nobody left those areas as a result of that fighting. And it's an exaggeration to say that there was hostilities between the two of them. They were hostile to one another, but there was no open fighting to the extent of coordinated and organised military action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And again you said to your knowledge no one left the area due to that. That's again based upon your interviews of 600 individuals who represent .03 of 1 per cent of the entire population?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The departure from Kosovo of 850.000 people was the result, based on my interviews, of a coordinated campaign to expel them. And at the time period we are referring to, which is from March to June 1999, by that point FARK and KLA had made up, if you will, had decided to cooperate with one another. So there was not tension and fighting between -- well, tension always existed but fighting and hostility between the two in the period of the NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, this is all based on your knowledge. And again if the KLA did pressure people not to talk about other reasons for leaving, then you would not have heard about them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, if -- are you telling me that if the KLA pressured people not to talk about other reasons you would somehow find out about that?

utterances.speaker: FRED ABRAHAMS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, that's your testimony. Now, let's move to the NATO attacks for which I believe you do have some knowledge and information from what I've read.
